quickAnswer: Oil heats 52.4% of Southborough homes against 36.5% in the middle town, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $740,000 (ACS 2022). Most replacement decisions here begin with oil against a heat pump.
body: ## Oil first, in a town of $740,000 houses

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) counts 1,886 of Southborough's 3,599 occupied homes on fuel oil or kerosene. That share, 52.4%, ranks 17th of the 50 MetroWest towns we serve; the middle town is at 36.5%. Utility gas heats 1,077 homes (29.9%), tank gas 301 (8.4%) and electricity 271 (7.5%).

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $740,000, the 12th highest of the 50 towns and far above the $579,150 for the middle town. At that value, a like-for-like oil boiler and a bigger project such as a heat pump are worth pricing side by side, and our written estimates are free before any work starts.
## Mostly detached houses, half of them older than 1980

Of 3,649 housing units, 3,069 (84.1%) are single-family detached houses, the 12th-highest share of the 50 towns. Only 339 units (9.3%) sit in multi-unit buildings. The median home was built in 1979, a little newer than the 1975 of the middle town, and 1,859 homes (50.9%) predate 1980. Renter households are 10.6% of the total, 40th-highest of the 50 towns, so most heating decisions here are made by owners. The town covers 15.7 square miles, of which 14.1 square miles is land.

- 448 homes (12.3%) date from 1939 or earlier.
- 523 (14.3%) were built from 1940 to 1959.
- 888 (24.3%) are from 1960 to 1979.
- 1,150 (31.5%) are from 1980 to 1999, the largest band.
- 640 (17.5%) are from 2000 on, and 223 of those (6.1%) from 2010 on.

Detached houses often get additions over the decades, and an old boiler may no longer suit the house around it. Older construction usually leaks more air than newer. Because we assess the heating load of your house before quoting, the size of the new system follows the building as it stands today, not the unit being removed.
## Reservoir, mills and Route 9

The Wikipedia history of Southborough says the town was first settled in 1660 and incorporated in July 1727, and that it was primarily a farming community until mills began to use the small rivers. In 1898 the Fayville Dam was built to create reservoirs for a growing Boston, and manufacturing vanished. The town did not see substantial growth until the high-tech boom of the 1970s. The MBTA Commuter Rail station in Cordaville opened on June 22, 2002, and Interstate 495 and the Massachusetts Turnpike both pass through town without an interchange inside its limits.

As of 2021, 43% of land use was residential and 35% was open space, including one-tenth of the town's area flooded by the Sudbury Reservoir. Light industrial use is concentrated along main roads, primarily Route 9. The town incorporates the villages of Cordaville, Fayville and Southville, with several small business districts in the villages and along Route 9, and Routes 30 and 85 also run through town. The public library dates from 1852, and the town has six public schools, four of them inside town limits.
## Electricity and the rebate path

Southborough sits in National Grid's Massachusetts Electric Company territory. Just 7.5% of homes heat with electricity, so a heat pump here would usually take over from oil, gas or propane. Rebate amounts and the weatherization test are laid out on the [heat pump page](/cities/southborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Is oil the most common heating fuel in Southborough?
faq.a: Yes. Oil or kerosene heats 1,886 of 3,599 occupied homes (52.4%), with utility gas next at 29.9%. If an oil boiler fails, a replacement estimate should compare a new oil system with a heat pump and, where a main is available, gas. Tank gas adds another 8.4%.

faq.q: Do Southborough homes qualify for Mass Save heat pump rebates?
faq.a: They can. National Grid, the electric utility here, is a Mass Save sponsor, and the main condition is that the house is sufficiently weatherized first. Of the town's units, 640 (17.5%) date from 2000 or later and pass on age alone. Amounts and dates change, so confirm them on the heat pump page and at masssave.com.

faq.q: How many Southborough households rent their home?
faq.a: Renters number 383 households, or 10.6%, which is 40th of the 50 towns, while 3,216 households (89.4%) own. Vacancy is 1.4%, 46th of 50. In practice the person deciding on a new boiler is usually the owner living in the house. Of the 3,649 housing units, 50 stand vacant.

faq.q: Half of Southborough homes were built before 1980. Does that change sizing?
faq.a: It can. With 50.9% of homes built before 1980, insulation and air sealing vary from house to house, and an upgraded envelope shrinks the heating load. That is why we assess your home's load before quoting, rather than copying the size of the old unit.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Utility gas reaches 1,077 Southborough homes and tank gas 301, while oil leads the town, so a failed boiler starts as a fuel question. The age of the house and a gas permit, where gas is involved, shape the rest.
body: ## Gas, oil or propane: settle the fuel first

Utility gas heats 1,077 homes here (29.9%), 32nd of the 50 towns and well under the 41.9% of the middle town. A gas main on your street is therefore not something to assume. When a boiler dies, the first job is to find out whether a main passes your house and what a conversion would involve compared with a like-for-like oil unit.
### Homes outside the gas network

Bottled or tank gas heats 301 homes (8.4%), 11th highest of the 50 towns, against 4.5% for the middle town. A tank is refilled by delivery, as an oil tank is, so a household on propane and one on oil face a similar question when the boiler ages: stay with the fuel or move to a heat pump.
### The permit step for gas equipment

Gas permits in Massachusetts go through licensed plumbers and gas fitters alone. A new gas furnace or boiler normally also needs a final inspection before it counts as done, and the building department can tell you what it requires for your street address.
### Sizing a replacement for a 1979 house

Southborough's median home was built in 1979, and 1,859 units (50.9%) predate 1980. In a house of that vintage the nameplate on the old boiler says little about what the building needs now, because windows, insulation and air sealing may have changed since it was installed. Our quote follows a heating-load assessment of the house, so the new unit matches the building as it stands.
### Mixed eras under one roof

Of the 1,859 units built before 1980, 888 date from 1960 to 1979, 523 from 1940 to 1959 and 448 from 1939 or earlier. The pipework, flue and chimney that a new boiler must connect to can therefore differ a great deal from one street to the next, which is one more reason to look at the house before choosing the unit.
### Next steps
If the heating system is only part of the question, the [maintenance page](/cities/southborough/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) covers how an oil burner is kept running between replacements.

faq.q: Can I switch from oil to gas in Southborough?
faq.a: Only where a gas main already serves your street. Utility gas heats 29.9% of the town's homes, a minority, so check your own address first. Then compare the connection work and the new equipment against a replacement oil unit or a heat pump before you decide.

faq.q: How do you size a boiler or furnace for an older house?
faq.a: We assess the home's heating load before quoting a system, instead of copying the size of the unit being removed. With half the town built before 1980, the walls, windows and air leakage of the actual house are what set the number.

faq.q: What if the heat quits at night?
faq.a: Call (508) 786-8755. We take emergency calls 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Before you call, check that the thermostat is set to heat, the switch at the equipment is on and, for an oil system, that the tank is not empty.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Detached houses are 84.1% of Southborough's housing, which leaves room outside for a condenser. Ducts are the open question, and a ductless mini-split can cool rooms that central air would not reach.
body: ## Cooling mostly detached houses

Of the town's 3,649 housing units, 3,069 are single-family detached, and that is the 12th highest share of the 50 towns. A detached house usually has a yard side for an outdoor condenser. Townhouse-style attached units total 241 (6.6%), buildings of five or more units 159 (4.4%), two-unit buildings 131 (3.6%) and buildings of three to four units 49 (1.3%).

With 339 units (9.3%) in multi-unit buildings and no mobile homes counted, most cooling jobs involve a house with its own yard rather than a shared roof or wall. A condenser also needs clearance from the house and from shrubs, so the outdoor spot is a planning item, not an afterthought.
### Ducts decide the system

Central air needs a duct network. Where a house has one, the question is whether it was sized and sealed for cooling as well as heating. Where heat comes from radiators or baseboard, there is nothing to borrow, and a ductless mini-split puts a single outdoor unit on the ground with a slim indoor head in each zone. Many older homes were built without central air, and the line set needs only a small opening in the wall.
### Reading the house before the equipment
A cooling plan usually turns on a few practical points:
- The rooms that run warmest in July, such as a top-floor bedroom.
- Where the condenser can stand and how long the line set has to run.
- Whether the electrical panel has room for another circuit.
- Whether one system for the whole house or separate zones suits the layout.
### One unit for both seasons

A heat pump cools as well as heats. For a house facing both a tired cooling system and an aging oil boiler, one heat pump project can replace two separate purchases. The [heat pump page](/cities/southborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) has the details.

faq.q: Can I add central air to a Southborough house with baseboard heat?
faq.a: You can, but it means building a duct network, which is a bigger job in a finished house. A ductless mini-split is often the simpler route because it needs no ductwork, only a small opening for the refrigerant line set and a spot outside for the condenser.

faq.q: Do I need to replace my condenser and furnace together?
faq.a: Not always, but it is worth looking at both. The indoor coil and the outdoor unit have to match, and with a median home built in 1979, an old furnace can be the next thing to fail. We would rather quote both than leave you facing a second job soon.

faq.q: Why does an air conditioner that is too big feel clammy?
faq.a: An oversized unit cools the air quickly and shuts off before it has pulled much moisture out, so the rooms feel damp. That is why we size cooling from the house itself, its rooms, windows and ducts, and not from the label on the old condenser.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: National Grid serves Southborough and is a Mass Save sponsor, so Mass Save rebates are the route. With oil in 1,886 homes and tank gas in 301, many households could swap a delivered fuel for electric heat.
body: ## A National Grid town with many delivered fuels

Southborough is in National Grid's Massachusetts Electric Company territory, and National Grid is a Mass Save sponsor. On the 2026 install window the whole-home rebate pays $2,650 per ton, capped at $8,500 per home, and weatherization comes first. The full rules sit on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Who has the most to gain

A heat pump replaces fuel that is bought by delivery or by the therm. The 1,886 oil and kerosene homes and the 301 tank gas homes are the obvious candidates. Electricity heats 271 homes (7.5%), 42nd of the 50 towns, and those households already pay for heat through the electric bill, so for them a heat pump is a different way to use the same utility.
### Age bands against the 2000 cutoff

The weatherization test counts a house built in 2000 or later as passed. Southborough has 640 such units (17.5%), so most of the housing falls on the other side of the line and needs the assessment route or completed recommendations. A Home Energy Assessment becomes the first step there, since it also shows where air sealing would shrink the load.
### Keeping a boiler as backup

A partial-home setup can leave the existing boiler in place for the coldest days, while a whole-home setup carries the whole load on its own. Which one fits is a question about the house, and we assess the heating load before quoting.
### Ducted or ductless

Where good ducts exist, a ducted unit can use them. Houses heated by radiators suit ductless heads in the rooms that matter. With 84.1% of units being detached houses, most projects will be in houses with room for outdoor equipment on the lot.

Where a house keeps a boiler and also has a separate cooling system, one heat pump setup can fold heating and cooling into a single project, which is worth pricing against replacing the two pieces one at a time.

faq.q: Does a house built in the 1980s need a Home Energy Assessment?
faq.a: Probably, yes. Age alone clears the test only for houses built in 2000 or later. A 1980s house can still qualify if an assessment recommends under $1,000 of work, or if recommendations made in 2013 or later were completed. The assessment is the usual way to show that.

faq.q: Can a heat pump replace an oil boiler here?
faq.a: It can, and cold-climate models are made for Massachusetts winters. Whether it carries the full load depends on the house, so we assess the heating load first. Some owners keep the boiler as a backup for the coldest days instead of removing it.

faq.q: I heat with propane. Is a heat pump worth a look?
faq.a: It is worth pricing. Tank gas is delivered like oil, and 8.4% of Southborough homes use it, among the highest shares of the 50 towns. A quote can set the cost of a new propane unit beside a heat pump that also provides cooling in summer.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Southborough's 1,886 oil-heated homes each need a yearly burner cleaning, and the median house, built in 1979, is more than four decades old. Owners outnumber renters 3,216 to 383, so most tune-ups are the homeowner's call.
body: ## A yearly visit for oil burners

A burner, nozzle, filter and set of combustion readings drift over one season, and soot collects inside a boiler or furnace that is not cleaned. In a town where oil is the leading fuel, a fall visit is the habit that matters most for those households.
### What the visit covers, by fuel
- Oil: clean the burner and heat exchanger, replace the filter and nozzle, test combustion and inspect the flue.
- Utility or tank gas: check the burner, the venting, the controls and the safety shutoffs.
- Heat pumps and air conditioners: clean coils and filters, read the refrigerant side and clear the condensate drain.

The Census also lists 37 homes on other fuel or coal and 6 on wood, so a handful of Southborough households have equipment that needs its own checks. Between visits, change filters on the schedule printed on the packaging, keep the space around a burner clear and brush snow away from an outdoor unit.
### Owners decide, mostly

The Census Bureau counts 3,216 owner households (89.4%) and 383 renter households (10.6%). Where a unit is rented, state rules put the heating bill on the landlord unless the lease says otherwise, which often makes the pre-winter visit the landlord's to book.
### Planning ahead on an older system

The median home here dates from 1979, and parts for older units can be harder to find. A tune-up is the right moment to ask how many seasons remain, so replacement is planned rather than forced in January.
### Timing
- Late summer or early fall for boilers and furnaces.
- Spring for central air and mini-splits.
- Any time you hear a new noise or smell something odd.

Households on bottled gas, 301 of them (8.4%), should have the tank connection and regulator looked at during the same visit, since a delivered fuel puts those parts in daily use. Gas customers on the utility network, 1,077 homes, mostly need the burner and venting checked.
If the visit shows the system is near the end of its life, the [heating page](/cities/southborough/heating-installation-repair) covers replacement.

faq.q: How often should an oil burner be cleaned in Southborough?
faq.a: Once a year, before the heating season starts. With oil in more than half of the town's homes, this is the service that matters most here. A skipped cleaning can let soot build up, which may lower efficiency and bring a breakdown in the coldest weeks.

Yes, though less than combustion equipment. Filters, coils and the condensate drain need regular attention, and a technician can read the refrigerant side of the system. Keep outdoor units clear of leaves and, after a storm, of snow, so air can move freely through them.

faq.q: Should a landlord or a tenant schedule the tune-up?
faq.a: Unless the lease says otherwise, the landlord pays for heat, so the landlord normally arranges the boiler service. Southborough has 383 renter households, a small group, but any of them can ask the owner to confirm the date of the last cleaning.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Southborough's housing runs from 448 units built in 1939 or earlier to 223 built since 2010. Old houses and tight new ones have different air problems, so the right fix starts with your own house's age.
body: ## One town, several ages of house

The 2022 ACS sorts the town's 3,649 units into age bands, and the largest, 1,150 units (31.5%), was built from 1980 to 1999. Water covers 9.64% of the town's total area, and indoors, moisture is worth watching in a house of any age. The bands matter because a house's age gives a first guess at how much air it exchanges with the outdoors.
### The oldest houses

The 448 units from 1939 or earlier tend to leak air through gaps. Some pollutants thin out that way, while dust, pollen and basement air get drawn in. Old ductwork can hold years of dust, and before renovating a house this old, a qualified specialist should test for older materials.
### The newest houses

The 223 units built since 2010 are usually tighter. That saves energy, but cooking fumes, moisture and chemicals from furnishings stay indoors unless ventilation keeps up. A mechanical fresh-air source can be part of the answer, and it is something to raise at the planning stage rather than after move-in.
### Basements and winter dryness

Dampness in a basement may come from the ground, a plumbing line or humid summer air hitting cool walls. A dehumidifier treats the air, not the cause. In winter the heating season dries the house, and a humidifier helps only if the setting stays modest, because water on cold windows is its own problem.

With 3,069 detached houses, most air problems are handled house by house, where a bath fan, a dryer vent or an attic hatch can matter as much as the filter. A walk through the house usually shows where moist or stale air collects, and the answer is often a small fix before it is a new machine.
### Where we can help
- Filtration, with filters changed on schedule.
- Humidity control for a damp basement or a dry winter.
- Ventilation for a tight house.
- Duct work where ducts are damaged.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. A technician can look inside, and cleaning is worth it when the ducts hold visible mold, dirt buildup or damage from pests or a renovation. A dusty register on its own is usually a filter question, so start there before paying for a full cleaning.

The moisture may be rising from the ground, leaking from a pipe or condensing from humid summer air on cool walls. Run a dehumidifier for comfort, but trace the source first, because a leak or poor grading outside needs a repair that no appliance replaces.

faq.q: Is a house from the 1980 to 1999 band leaky or tight?
faq.a: Somewhere in between. That band is the town's largest at 31.5% of units, and houses of that era are generally tighter than pre-1940 ones but looser than new construction. Only a test of the actual house tells you, and the result guides whether a ventilator makes sense.
